- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at +3–5% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion or rebound bias.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts — smooth out 3–5 day moving average of forecast to reduce noise.
- In 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture true mean reversion — if 18-day history shows strong mean reversion, forecast should align with 18-day average ± 2%.
- When sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model tends to project upward — adjust downward 1–3% if sentiment >0.67 and price <10% above 18-day avg.
- If sentiment is low and price is rising, model underestimates — add 1–2% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven momentum.
